scientific_objective: Test whether missing snow processes and parameter compensation in hydrological models (Base vs CN vs TGD2) produce divergent downstream shared soil-water state trajectories in real catchments, and whether explicit snow physics improves consistency against external soil-state references along a snow-burden gradient.

external_soil_reference.source: Caravan v1.1 CAMELS-US subset (ERA5-Land hourly basin-averaged, non-DST local standard time)
external_soil_reference.semantics: external process-state consistency reference; NOT ground-truth soil moisture

component_stores.wu: upper layer tension water store (capacity um)
component_stores.wl: lower layer tension water store (capacity lm)
component_stores.wd: deep layer tension water store (capacity dm)

comparability_principles: NO absolute storage comparison (mm vs m3/m3 is physically non-convertible)
NO 1-to-1 depth horizon mapping between conceptual XAJ layers and physical ERA5-Land layers
Evaluate standardized dynamics, seasonal correlations, deseasonalized anomaly correlations, and seasonal recharge timing

timing_diagnostics.soil_peak_timing: day-of-water-year (Oct 1 = 1) of annual maximum soil moisture / W_total
timing_diagnostics.spring_wetup_timing: day-of-water-year of maximum 14-day soil moisture increase (recharge onset)

snow_burden_environmental_axes.primary: Snow-17 ensemble median annual maximum SWE [mm] over WY 1996..2010 (r4_swe_reference_v1)
snow_burden_environmental_axes.secondary_duration: Snow-17 median SWE-positive days over WY 1996..2010

paired_effects.primary_contrast: Delta(CN - Base) = Consistency(CN) - Consistency(Base) per basin
statistical_methods: Spearman rank correlation rho vs snow burden
Nonparametric basin-level bootstrap 95% CI (2000 replicates, fixed seed 20260730)
